title: Temurah 8
description: Rav Naḥman’s ruling that the priest has no acquisition in an unblemished firstborn while the Temple stands is tested against a baraita on “you shall not redeem,” a priestess’s child mixed up with her maidservant’s, the idolatrous city, the denied deposit and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri; then Rav Ḥisda and Rav Huna explain why a priest may not sell a firstborn to an Israelite, and Mar Zutra questions the firstborn meat served at Rav Ashi’s house.
topics: 🐑 “You shall not redeem … but it may be sold”: which clause is about a blemished firstborn
👶 A priestess’s child mixed up with her maidservant’s: why their firstborns graze
🏚️ The idolatrous city: what “its animals” and “its spoil” leave out
⚖️ Denying a deposit of offerings: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, Ben Azzai and Abba Yosei ben Dosai
🌍 Abaye and Ravina: a firstborn from outside Eretz Yisrael, following Rabbi Shimon
🔄 Substitution in the owner’s house and in the priest’s house
🌾 Selling a firstborn to an Israelite: “a priest who assists at the threshing floor”
🍖 Mar Zutra at Rav Ashi’s: firstborn meat bought from a priest

a1.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: בִּבְכוֹר נֶאֱמַר ״לֹא תִפְדֶּה״ וְנִמְכָּר הוּא, בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה — אֵימָא סֵיפָא: ״וְאֶת דָּמָם תִּזְרוֹק עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״, בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה מִי אִיכָּא מִזְבֵּחַ? אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.

a2.he: וּבְמַאי? אִילֵימָא בְּבַעַל מוּם — אֵימָא סֵיפָא: ״וְאֶת דָּמָם תִּזְרוֹק עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר״ — מִי חֲזֵי לְהַקְרָבָה?! אֶלָּא לָאו בְּתָם, וְקָתָנֵי נִמְכָּר הוּא, אַלְמָא אִית לְהוּ לְכֹהֵן זְכִיָּיה בְּגַוֵּיהּ!

a3.he: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? רֵישָׁא — בְּבַעַל מוּם, סֵיפָא — בְּתָם.

a4.he: מֵתִיב רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: כֹּהֶנֶת שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵבה וְלָדָהּ בִּוְלַד שִׁפְחָתָהּ, הִגְדִּילוּ הַתַּעֲרוֹבוֹת — מְשַׁחְרְרִין זֶה אֶת זֶה, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אוֹכְלִין בִּתְרוּמָה, וְחוֹלְקִין חֵלֶק אֶחָד עַל הַגּוֹרֶן. בְּכוֹרָן יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ, וְיֵאָכְלוּ בְּמוּמָן.

a5.he: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה — מַאי שְׁנָא דִּידַן וּמַאי שְׁנָא דִּידְהוּ? דִּידַן נָמֵי מוּמִין בָּעֵינַן! אֶלָּא לָאו בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים? אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא אִית לְהוּ לְכֹהֵן זְכִיָּיה בְּגַוֵּויהּ — שַׁפִּיר, אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לֵית לֵיהּ — לֵיתֵי גִּזְבָּר וְלִישְׁקְלֵהּ!

a6.he: לְעוֹלָם בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, וּדְקָא קַשְׁיָא לָךְ: מַאי שְׁנָא דִּידַן וּמַאי שְׁנָא דִּידְהוּ? אֲנַן יָהֲבִינַן לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן בְּמוּמַיְיהוּ, אִינְהוּ — כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא בְּהוּ מִקְצָת כֹּהֵן, מַפְקַע לֵיהּ לְכֹהֲנִים.

a7.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, מַאי אִירְיָא בְּכוֹרוֹת דְּהָלֵין סְפֵיקוֹת? אֲפִילּוּ דִּידַן נָמֵי יִרְעוּ! אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים, וְאִי בְּבַעַל מוּם — יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ? הָא מְסוֹאָבִין וְקָיְימִין! אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּתַמִּין, וְהָכִי הוּא דְּלָא מְזַבְּנִי וַדַּאי.

a8.he: לְעוֹלָם בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, מַאי קַשְׁיָא לָךְ, אֲפִילּוּ דִּילַן נָמֵי יִרְעוּ? לָא (מָצִינוּ) [מָצֵינַן] מְדַחֵינַן לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן, דְּלָא אִית כָּאן סְפֵק כְּהוּנָּה. הָנֵי סְפֵיקוֹת מְדַחוּ לְכֹהֵן, כֹּל חַד וְחַד אָמַר לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן: דַּאֲנָא כֹּהֵן וַאֲנָא כֹּהֵן.

a9.he: מֵיתִיבִי: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: ״בְּהֶמְתָּהּ״ — פְּרָט לְבֶהֱמַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁבָּהּ, ״שְׁלָלָהּ״ — פְּרָט לְכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁבָּהּ.

a10.he: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה — מִי אִיכָּא עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת? וְהָתְנַן: אֵין עוֹשִׂין עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד! אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.

a11.he: וּבְמַאי? אִי נֵימָא בְּבַעַל מוּם — הַיְינוּ ״בְּהֶמְתָּהּ״! אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּתָם. וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא אִית לֵיהּ זְכִיָּיה בְּגַוֵּיהּ — שַׁפִּיר, אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לֵית לֵיהּ — לְמָה לִי מִבְּהֵמָה? תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִ״שְּׁלָלָהּ״, וְלֹא שְׁלַל שָׁמַיִם!

a12.he: לְעוֹלָם בְּבַעַל מוּם, וּדְקָא קַשְׁיָא לָךְ הַיְינוּ ״בְּהֶמְתָּהּ״ — מִי שֶׁנֶּאֱכָל בְּתוֹרַת ״בְּהֶמְתָּהּ״, יָצְאוּ בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר (שֶׁאֵינוֹ בִּכְלַל) [שֶׁאֵין נֶאֱכָלִין בְּתוֹרַת] ״בְּהֶמְתָּהּ״.

a13.he: דִּתְנַן: כׇּל פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין נִמְכָּרִין בָּאִיטְלִיז, וְנִשְׁחָטִין בָּאִיטְלִיז, וְנִשְׁקָלִין בְּלִיטְרָא, חוּץ מִן הַבְּכוֹר וּמִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁהֲנָאָתָן לַבְּעָלִים.

a14.he: מֵיתִיבִי: ״וּמָעֲלָה מַעַל בַּה׳״ — לְרַבּוֹת קֳדָשִׁים קַלִּים, שֶׁהֵן מָמוֹן בְּעָלִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי.

a15.he: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: לְרַבּוֹת שְׁלָמִים. אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסַאי אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי אֶלָּא בִּבְכוֹר בִּלְבָד.

a16.he: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה — הָא דּוּמְיָא דִּשְׁלָמִים קָתָנֵי! אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.

a17.he: וּבְמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּבַעַל מוּם — הָא דּוּמְיָא דִּשְׁלָמִים קָתָנֵי! אֶלָּא לָאו בְּתָם, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אִית לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן זְכִיָּיה בְּגַוֵּויהּ.

b1.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא, לְעוֹלָם בְּתָם, וּבִבְכוֹר בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא דְּאָמַר: אִם בָּאוּ תְּמִימִין יִקְרְבוּ.

b2.he: מֵיתִיבִי: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי: מָה לִי אִם אֵינוֹ מֵימֵר בְּחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם, שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין זָכִין בָּהֶן בְּחַיֵּיהֶן, תֹּאמַר בִּבְכוֹר שֶׁזָּכִין בְּחַיָּיו. בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּבַעַל מוּם — הָא דּוּמְיָא דְּחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם קָאָמַר, אֶלָּא לָאו בְּתָם, וְקָתָנֵי זָכִין בּוֹ בְּחַיָּיו!

b3.he: אָמַר רָבִינָא: הָא נָמֵי בִּבְכוֹר בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דְּאָמַר: אִם בָּאוּ תְּמִימִים — יִקְרְבוּ.

b4.he: לֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי: בְּכוֹר, בְּבֵית הַבְּעָלִים — עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, בְּבֵית הַכֹּהֵן — אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁבָּא לִידֵי כֹהֵן — אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה.

b5.he: הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא! מַאי לָאו הָכִי קָאָמַר: בְּבֵית כֹּהֵן — הוּא עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, וְאֵין בַּעַל עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, אַלְמָא אִית לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן זְכִיָּיה בְּגַוֵּויהּ.

b6.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי, הָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.

b7.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא כֹּהֵן לְכֹהֵן, אֲבָל כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל — אָסוּר. מַאי טַעְמָא? דִּלְמָא אָזֵיל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא, וּמַמְטֵי לְחָכָם, וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ: ״בְּכוֹר זֶה נָתַן לִי כֹּהֵן בְּמוּמוֹ״.

b8.he: וּמִי שָׁרֵי חָכָם הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַב: אֵין רוֹאִין בְּכוֹר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן כֹּהֵן עִמּוֹ!

b9.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּכֹהֵן הַמְסַיֵּיעַ בְּבֵית הַגֳּרָנוֹת.

b10.he: מָר זוּטְרָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי. אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: לִטְעוֹם מָר מִידֵּי. אַיְיתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ בִּישְׂרָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֵיכוֹל מָר, דְּמַיבְרֵי מִשּׁוּם דְּבוּכְרָא הוּא. מְנָא לְכוּ הָא? אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: דְּזַבֵּן לַן פְּלוֹנִי כֹּהֵן.

b11.he: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָא סְבִירָא לְכוּ הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּכֹהֵן הַמְסַיֵּיעַ בְּבֵית הַגֳּרָנוֹת? אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: לָא סְבִירָא לַן, דַּאֲנַן מִיזְבָּן קָא זָבְנִינַן.

b12.he: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וְלָא סְבִירָא לְכוּ הָדִתְנַן: עַד כַּמָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּיב לִיטַּפֵּל בַּבְּכוֹר? בַּדַּקָּה — שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, ובגסה — חמשים יום. וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: ״תְּנֵהוּ לִי בְּתוֹךְ זְמַנּוֹ״ — הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִתְּנֶנּוּ לוֹ. וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מָה טַעַם? מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּכֹהֵן הַמְסַיֵּיעַ בְּבֵית הַגֳּרָנוֹת!

b13.he: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הָתָם מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא, הָכָא מִזְבָּן קָא זָבְנִינַן.

b14.he: לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הָכָא לָא יָהֵיב דְּמֵי, הָכָא קָא יָהֵיב דְּמֵי. מַאי אָמְרַתְּ? מוֹזֵיל כֹּהֵן גַּבֵּיהּ, דְּסָבַר כֹּהֵן דְּכִי הָוֵי לֵיהּ בְּכוֹר אַחֲרִינָא יָהֵיב נִיהֲלֵיהּ? לָא, דְּמַסֵּיק אַדַּעְתֵּיהּ:

messages.text: 8a

Continued from 7b: Rav Naḥman, citing Rabba bar Avuh, taught that the mishna’s permission to sell an unblemished firstborn alive applies only in the present, when the priest has acquisition in it; while the Temple is standing, the unblemished firstborn stands for sacrifice and may not be sold. Rava raised one objection from that mishna and Rav Naḥman answered it. Now Rava raises another.

With regard to a firstborn offering, it is stated: “But the firstling of an ox, or the firstling of a sheep, or the firstling of a goat, you shall not redeem; they are holy: And you shall sprinkle their blood against the altar”. But it may be sold to another priest for consumption after its sacrifice.
messages.lead: Rava raised an objection to the statement of Rav Naḥman from a baraita:

verse.he: אַךְ בְּכוֹר־שׁוֹר אוֹ־בְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב אוֹ־בְכוֹר עֵז לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם אֶת־דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת־חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But the firstlings of cattle, sheep, or goats may not be redeemed; they are consecrated. You shall dash their blood against the altar, and turn their fat into smoke as an offering by fire for a pleasing odor to GOD.

notes.he: פדיון אין לו שיכנס הפדיון בקדושה והוא יצא לחולין:
notes.en: With regard to a firstborn it is stated, “you shall not redeem”: it has no redemption by which the redemption money would take on its sanctity and it would go out to non-sacred status.

notes.he: ונאכל בקדושה וזו היא קדושה שלא ישחטנו באיטליז ולא ישקלנו בליטרא:
notes.en: But it may be sold: and it is eaten in sanctity. And this is its sanctity: that one may not slaughter it in the butchers’ market and may not weigh it by the litra.

notes.he: דלעולם הוא בקדושתו לענין דאינו נמכר באיטליז ואין נשקל בליטרא:
notes.en: With regard to a firstborn it is stated, “you shall not redeem”: meaning that it always remains in its sanctity, in that it is not sold in the butchers’ market and not weighed by the litra.

notes.dh: (אם) בבכור נאמר בו לא תפדה ונמכר הוא
notes.he: דכהן מוכר אותו דהא לא כתיב ביה לא לא ימכר ולא לא יגאל:
notes.en: With regard to a firstborn it is stated, “you shall not redeem,” but it may be sold: for the priest sells it, since neither “it shall not be sold” nor “it shall not be redeemed” is written regarding it.

messages.text: What era are we dealing with in this baraita? If we say it is in the present, say the latter clause of the verse: “And you shall sprinkle their blood against the altar.” Is there an altar in the present? Rather, it is obvious that it is referring to the time when the Temple is standing.

notes.he: דקרא דלא תפדה:
notes.en: Say the latter clause: of the verse of “you shall not redeem.”

notes.dh: אימא סיפא את דמם תזרוק על המזבח
notes.he: אסיפא דקרא קאמר:
notes.en: Say the latter clause: “And you shall sprinkle their blood against the altar”: he is referring to the latter clause of the verse.

messages.text: And what sort of animal are we dealing with here? If we say that it is referring to a blemished animal, say the latter clause of the verse: “And you shall sprinkle their blood against the altar, and burn their fat.” Is a blemished animal fit for sacrifice? Rather, is it not referring to an unblemished animal? And the baraita teaches that it may be sold. Evidently, the priest has the right of acquisition to an unblemished firstborn offering even when the Temple is standing and the animal must be sacrificed.

Are the two clauses of the verse comparable? The first clause is stated with regard to a blemished animal, and it is teaching that it may be sold, and the latter clause is stated with regard to an unblemished animal, and it teaches that it is sacrificed as an offering. Unblemished animals may not be sold when the Temple is standing.
messages.lead: Rav Naḥman responds:
messages.quote: say the latter clause of the verse

notes.he: להכי דייקינן ונמכר הוא וסופיה דכתיב ואת דמם תזרוק בתם:
notes.en: The first clause of the verse is with regard to a blemished animal: that is why we infer “but it may be sold”; and its latter clause, where it is written “and you shall sprinkle their blood,” is with regard to an unblemished one.

notes.he: ודקא קשיא לך מי איכא ואת דמם תזרוק לעולם בבעל מום עסקי' ובזמן שבית המקדש קיים ולא קשיא רישיה דקרא דכתיב לא תפדה ואמרינן דנמכר הוא בבעל מום דתניא וסיפיה ואת דמם תזרוק בתם קמיירי:
notes.en: Actually when the Temple is standing. And as for what is difficult for you, is there “and you shall sprinkle their blood”? Actually we are dealing with a blemished animal when the Temple is standing, and it is not difficult: the first clause of the verse, where it is written “you shall not redeem,” and we say that it may be sold, is with regard to a blemished animal, as is taught; and its latter clause, “and you shall sprinkle their blood,” is speaking of an unblemished one.

messages.text: In the case of a priestess’s offspring who was comingled with her maidservant’s offspring, when the comingled children have grown up, they free each other, and therefore whichever one was a slave will be emancipated. And even beforehand, they both may partake of teruma, as both a priest and the slave of a priest may partake of teruma.
messages.lead: Rav Mesharshiyya raises an objection from a mishna:

notes.he: ואין יודע אי זה כהן ואי זה עבד:
notes.en: With her maidservant’s offspring: and it is not known which one is the priest and which one is the slave.

notes.he: כל אחד ואחד כותב אם אני הרב ואתה העבד הרי אתה בן חורין ויהיו מותרים שניהן בבת ישראל:
notes.en: They free each other: each one writes, “If I am the master and you are the slave, you are hereby a free man,” and then both will be permitted to marry a Jewish woman.

notes.he: כל זמן שלא שחררו זה את זה דעבד כהן נמי אכיל בתרומה:
notes.en: And they both partake of teruma: as long as they have not freed each other, since the slave of a priest also eats teruma.

notes.he: הגדילו התערובות הרי אוכלין בתרומה ממה נפשך דכל חד אמר אם כהן אני תנו לי בשביל עצמי אם עבד כהן אני הרי מותר בתרומה:
notes.en: The comingled ones grew up; they eat teruma either way, since each one says: If I am a priest, give to me for my own sake; if I am a priest’s slave, I am permitted to eat teruma.

messages.text: And they receive one share of teruma in the granary, because the slave of a priest receives no share. And their firstborn animals must graze until they become unfit for sacrifice by virtue of a blemish, and then they may be eaten with their blemish.

notes.he: כלומר כששניהן ביחד נותנין להן תרומה בבית הגרנות אבל לאחד מהן אין חולקין עד שיבוא חבירו דשמא זה הוא העבד. וסבירא ליה להאי תנא דאין חולקין תרומה לעבד אלא אם כן רבו עמו דילמא אתי לאסוקיה ליוחסין:
notes.en: And they receive one share in the granary: that is to say, when the two are together, teruma is given to them at the threshing floors; but to one of them alone no share is given until his fellow comes, since perhaps this one is the slave. And this tanna holds that teruma is not distributed to a slave unless his master is with him, lest people come to raise him to [priestly] lineage.

notes.he: של הני תערובות אם נולד בכור בהמה בעדרן ירעה כו' כדמפרש:
notes.en: And their firstborn: of these comingled ones. If a firstborn animal was born in their flock, it grazes, etc., as [the Gemara] explains.

notes.dh: ונוטלין חלק אחד על הגורן דחד הוי כהן לחוד]
notes.he: ותני עלה דההוא בכורות של אלו תערובות אינן רשאין למוכרן דאין רשאי למכור בכור אלא כהן ודאי אלא ירעו עד שיסתאבו ויאכלו במומן לבעלים דאע"ג דחד מנייהו לא הוי כהן מצי למיכליה דהא לא אסור בכור למיכליה במומו לישראל ולא כהן דעלמ' מצי למיפקיה מדידהו דכל חד וחד מצי אמר ליה אייתי ראיה דלאו כהן אנא ושקליה:
notes.en: And they take one share in the granary, [since only one of them is a priest]. And it is taught concerning this that the firstborns of these comingled ones may not be sold, for only a definite priest may sell a firstborn; rather, they graze until they become unfit and are eaten with their blemish by the owners. For even though one of them is not a priest, he may eat it, since a firstborn with its blemish is not forbidden to an Israelite to eat; and no other priest can take it out of their [hands], since each one of them can say to him: Bring proof that I am not a priest, and take it.

messages.text: What era are we dealing with in this mishna? If we say it is in the present, what is different about our firstborn offerings, i.e., those of Israelites, and what is different about their firstborn offerings, those of priests? Ours also require that they have blemishes before they may be eaten. Why is the halakha stated specifically with regard to priests?
messages.quote: their firstborn animals must graze until they become unfit

notes.dh: מאי שנא דידן מדידהו דידן נמי
notes.he: אין לו תקנה עד שיומם. והשתא מאן דקא מותיב לא אסיק אדעתיה סיפא דקתני יאכל במומו לבעלים ואילו דידן הוה יהבינן ליה לכהן במומו ורב נחמן משני לה הכי במסקנא דמילתא:
notes.en: What is different about ours from theirs? Ours too: have no remedy until they are blemished. At this point the one raising the objection had not considered the latter clause, which teaches that it is eaten with its blemish by the owners, whereas ours we would give to a priest with its blemish. And Rav Naḥman answers it this way at the conclusion of the matter.

notes.dh: אי בזמן הזה מאי שנא דידן ומאי שנא דידהו
notes.he: כלומר הא כל בכורות דכולי עלמא נמי מומין בעינן דלא מתאכלי אלא במומיהן:
notes.en: If in the present, what is different about ours and what is different about theirs? That is to say, all the firstborns of everyone also require blemishes, since they are eaten only with their blemishes.

messages.text: Rather, is it not speaking of the time when the Temple is standing? Granted, if you say that the priest has the right of acquisition to an unblemished firstborn offering when the Temple is standing, it is well. But if you say that a priest does not have the right of acquisition, let the Temple treasurer [gizbar] come and take the firstborn offerings for sacrifice. Why are they left in the offspring’s possession until they develop blemishes?

notes.he: ודידן הוה יהבינן לכהן לאקרוביה ואילו דידהו זכי להו אע"ג דכהן נמי חייבת בהמתו בבכורה כדאמרינן בבכורות בפרק שני במשנה (דף יג.) לא נפטרו אלא מפדיון הבן ופטר חמור הני ירעו משום דבשאר בכורות כהן אינו מפסיד כלום שמקריב הוא עצמו את אימורי בכור ואוכלו אבל הני דאיכא חד דזר אי הוי יהביה בכורם לאקרוביה תו לא אכלי מיניה דבכור תם בזמן המקדש אינו נאכל לזרים כדאמרינן באיזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נו:) הבכור נאכל לכהנים הלכך ירעה ולכשיסתאב יאכלנו במומו דכל חד וחד אמר לכהן אני כהן ובכור אני אוכלנו דכיון דנפל בו מום אין בו אלא איסור גזל והכא איסור גזל נמי ליכא דשמא זה כהן וזכה בו והמוציא מחבירו עליו הראייה:
notes.en: Rather, is it not when the Temple is standing: and ours we would give to the priest to sacrifice, whereas theirs they acquire for themselves. Even though a priest’s animal is also subject to the firstborn obligation, as we say in Bekhorot, in the mishna of the second chapter (13a), [that priests and Levites] were exempted only from the redemption of the son and of the firstborn donkey, these graze. For with other firstborns a priest loses nothing, since he himself sacrifices the sacrificial portions of the firstborn and eats it. But with these, where one of them is a non-priest, if he gave their firstborn to be sacrificed they could no longer eat of it, since an unblemished firstborn while the Temple stands is not eaten by non-priests, as we say in Eizehu Mekoman (Zevaḥim 56b): the firstborn is eaten by priests. Therefore it grazes, and when it becomes unfit he eats it with its blemish, since each one says to the priest: I am a priest, and I will eat the firstborn. For once a blemish has befallen it, there is only the prohibition of robbery; and here there is not even a prohibition of robbery, since perhaps this one is a priest and acquired it, and the burden of proof rests on the one who seeks to take from his fellow.

notes.he: משום הכי יש בידו כח לשהותו ולומר שמא כהן אני וזכיתי בו תחילה ולא אתננו לכהן ואמתין עד שאוכל לאוכלו:
notes.en: Well: for this reason he has the power to keep it and say: perhaps I am a priest and acquired it first, and I will not give it to a priest; and I will wait until I can eat it.

notes.he: לכהן זכייה בבכור מחיים אמאי שבקינן ליה לאפקועיה ממזבח ליתי גזבר ולשקליה וליתביה לכהן מעליא דהא אין בו זכייה אלא ממזבח ואילך אלא ודאי אית ליה זכייה מחיים בבכור תם דהא ודאי בתם קמיירי דקתני ירעו עד שיסתאבו:
notes.en: But if you say it does not: if the priest has no acquisition in a firstborn during its lifetime, why do we let him remove it from the altar? Let the treasurer come and take it and give it to a proper priest, since there is no acquisition in it except from the altar onward. Rather, he certainly has acquisition during its lifetime in an unblemished firstborn, for it is certainly speaking of an unblemished one, since it teaches: they graze until they become unfit.

notes.he: אלא לאו בזמן שבית המקדש קיים מיירי ואי אמרת בשלמא דבכורות דעלמ' דכהנים גמורין אית לכהן זכייה בגויה דמצי מזבין ליה שפיר היינו דאיכא בין כהנים ודאין דידן להני תערובות דידהו דאינהו לא מצי מזבין לבכור דידיה אלא ירעה עד שיסתאב אלא אי אמרת דכהנים לית להו זכייה בגויה למזבניה דלא הוי דידהו אלא דמזבח כל שכן הני דספקות נינהו דלית להו זכייה בגויה כלל כלל וליתי גזבר ולישקליה וליקרביה למזבח:
notes.en: Rather, is it not speaking of when the Temple is standing? And granted, if you say that with ordinary firstborns of full priests the priest has acquisition in it, so that he can sell it, it is well: this is the difference between definite priests, ours, and these comingled ones, theirs, who cannot sell their firstborn; rather, it grazes until it becomes unfit. But if you say that priests have no acquisition in it to sell it, since it is not theirs but the altar’s, all the more so these, who are uncertain, have no acquisition in it at all; so let the treasurer come and take it and sacrifice it on the altar.

messages.text: Actually, the mishna is speaking of the present. And as for that which is difficult for you: What is different about our firstborn offerings and what is different about their firstborn offerings, there is in fact a difference, as we must give ours to a priest once they are blemished. Although it is permitted for Israelites to eat blemished firstborn offerings, they are still required to give them to priests.

notes.he: ומשום הכי ירעה דלא חזי להקרבה וזכה בו מחיים ודידן יהבינן להו לכהנים במומייהו דאע"ג דהומם ומותר לזרים מיהו איסור גזל איכא אבל הנך תערובות ליכא איסור גזל דכל חד אומר אני כהן וזוכה אני בו וממון המוטל בספק הוא והמוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה:
notes.en: Actually in the present: and for this reason it grazes, since it is not fit for sacrifice, and he acquired it during its lifetime. And ours we give to the priests with their blemishes, for even though it has been blemished and is permitted to non-priests, there is still the prohibition of robbery. But with these comingled ones there is no prohibition of robbery, since each one says: I am a priest and I acquire it. It is money whose ownership is in doubt, and the burden of proof rests on the one who seeks to take from his fellow.

messages.text: By contrast, they, the offspring mentioned in the mishna, are different, since there is part of a priest in each of them due to the uncertainty of their parentage. And this is sufficient to dislodge the claims of all other priests to the animal.

notes.he: לעולם בזמן הזה [עסקי' והא] דאמרת דידן נמי בעי מומין איכא בין דידן לדידהו דבכורות דידן יהבינן לכהן אבל אינהו [מצי] מדחי לכהן. בלישנא אחרינא מפרש טפי:
notes.en: Actually we are dealing [with the present]; and as for what you said, ours too require blemishes: there is a difference between ours and theirs, since our firstborns we give to the priest, but they [can] fend off the priest. The alternative version explains it more fully.

messages.text: If the mishna is referring to the present, why specifically discuss the firstborn offerings of these cases of uncertain parentage? Even our firstborn offerings should be left to graze until they are blemished. Rather, it is obvious that the mishna is referring to the time when the Temple is standing.
messages.lead: The Gemara presents an alternative version of the previous discussion:

messages.text: And if the mishna is speaking of a blemished animal, does it make sense to say: They should graze until they become unfit for sacrifice? They are already unfit. Rather, it is obvious that the mishna is referring to unblemished animals, and it is only in a case such as this, when the owners might not be priests, that they definitely may not sell the animal. One can infer that a priest may sell an unblemished firstborn offering when the Temple is standing.

Actually, the mishna is referring to the present. What is difficult for you, the fact that even our firstborn offerings should graze until they are blemished? We Israelites are unable to deny the priest who claims the firstborn offering, as there is no member of the priesthood, however uncertain, here among the owners of the animal.

By contrast, in these cases of uncertain parentage described in the mishna, they can deny the priest, as both of them can say to the priest: I am a priest, and I am a priest. Since the burden of proof rests upon the claimant, both may keep their animals until they are blemished.

A verse discussing an idolatrous city states: “You shall smite the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, destroying it utterly, and all that is therein and its animals, with the edge of the sword. And you shall gather all its spoil into the midst of the broad place thereof, and shall burn with fire the city, and all the spoil thereof”.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita (Tosefta, Sanhedrin 4:5):

verse.he: הַכֵּה תַכֶּה אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא לְפִי־חָרֶב הַחֲרֵם אֹתָהּ וְאֶת־כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּהּ וְאֶת־בְּהֶמְתָּהּ לְפִי־חָרֶב׃ וְאֶת־כׇּל־שְׁלָלָהּ תִּקְבֹּץ אֶל־תּוֹךְ רְחֹבָהּ וְשָׂרַפְתָּ בָאֵשׁ אֶת־הָעִיר וְאֶת־כׇּל־שְׁלָלָהּ כָּלִיל לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהָיְתָה תֵּל עוֹלָם לֹא תִבָּנֶה עוֹד׃
verse.en: put the inhabitants of that town to the sword and put its cattle to the sword. Doom it and all that is in it to destruction: gather all its spoil into the open square, and burn the town and all its spoil as a holocaust to the ETERNAL your God. And it shall remain an everlasting ruin, never to be rebuilt.

messages.text: The term “its animals” serves to exclude firstborn kosher animals and the animal tithe that are in the city, as they are sacred. The term “its spoil” serves to exclude money used to redeem the second tithe that is found in the city, as it too is sacred.

notes.he: גבי עיר הנדחת כתיב (דברים יג) ואת בהמתה לפי חרב. בהמתה משמע בהמה דידה שאין לגבוה חלק בה:
notes.en: Its animals: regarding the idolatrous city it is written: “And its animals, with the edge of the sword” (Deuteronomy 13:16). “Its animals” implies an animal that is its own, in which the Most High has no share.

notes.he: ואליבא דמ"ד מעשר שני ממון גבוה הוא:
notes.en: To exclude the money of second tithe in it: and this follows the one who says that second tithe is the property of the Most High.

notes.he: [בהמתה דכתיב בעיר הנדחת דכתיב החרם אותה ואת כל אשר בה ואת בהמתה פרט לבהמת בכור ומעשר שיש בה שיש לגבוה חלק בהם]:
notes.en: [“Its animals,” written regarding the idolatrous city, where it is written “destroying it utterly, and all that is therein and its animals”: excluding an animal of firstborn and tithe in it, in which the Most High has a share.]

messages.text: What era are we dealing with in this baraita? If we say it is in the present, can there be an idolatrous city in the present day?
A city may be designated as an idolatrous city only in accordance with the ruling of a court of seventy-one judges, i.e., the Great Sanhedrin?
messages.lead: But didn’t we learn in a mishna:

notes.he: בפ"ק דסנהדרין מפרש טעמא:
notes.en: One designates an idolatrous city only, etc.: the reason is explained in the first chapter of Sanhedrin.

messages.text: Rather, it is obvious that the mishna is referring to the period when the Temple is standing.

And to what type of animal is the baraita referring? If you say that it is referring to a blemished firstborn animal, which belongs to its owners, this is included in the term “its animals,” which one is commanded to destroy. Rather, it is obvious that the baraita is referring to an unblemished firstborn offering.
messages.quote: “its animals” serves to exclude firstborn kosher animals

notes.he: דכהן אוכל את הבכור וישראל את המעשר ואין לגבוה חלק בהן:
notes.en: This is “its animals”: for the priest eats the firstborn and the Israelite the tithe, and the Most High has no share in them.

notes.dh: ובמאי אילימא בבעל מום היינו בהמתה
notes.he: ואם תאמר לימא דאתיא כרבנן דאמרי דלאו ממוניה הוא וי"ל דעיקר הקושיא אינה אלא ממעשר דלכ"ע בעל מום ממוניה הוא. הרמ"ה:
notes.en: And with what? If we say with a blemished one, this is “its animals”: And if you say: let him say that it follows the Rabbis, who say that [a blemished firstborn] is not his property? One can say that the main difficulty is only from the tithe, for according to everyone a blemished one is his property. [So writes] the Rema [Rabbi Meir HaLevi Abulafia].

notes.he: היינו בהמתה דפסול חלק של גבוה למזבח [ואי אמרת לית ליה לכהן זכייה בגויה ולא מצי מזבין ליה משום חלק של גבוה]:
notes.en: If with a blemished firstborn, this is “its animals,” since the share of the Most High, for the altar, is disqualified. [And if you say that the priest has no acquisition in it and cannot sell it, because of the share of the Most High.]

messages.text: And granted, if you say that the priest has the right of acquisition to an unblemished firstborn offering when the Temple is standing, it is well, as although it belongs to an individual, the Torah nevertheless exempts it from destruction. But if you say that a priest does not have the right of acquisition, why do I need to derive its exemption from the term “its animals”? One should derive its exemption from the term “its spoil,” from which one can infer: But not the spoils of Heaven.

notes.he: משום הכי איצטריך קרא למעוטיה דלא נפיק משללה ולא שלל שמים דהאי לאו שלל שמים הוא דזכה כהן בגוויה. ל"א אלא פשיטא בתם והא ממעט לה מתורת בהמתה אלמא ממונא דכהן הוא ומיפרשא נמי כלישנא קמא דמדאיצטריך למכתב בהמתה ולא נפקא ליה משללה שמע מינה אית ליה לכהן זכייה בגויה מחיים:
notes.en: Well: for this reason a verse was needed to exclude it, since it is not excluded by “its spoil,” and not the spoils of Heaven; for this is not the spoils of Heaven, since the priest has acquired it. Another version: rather, it is obvious that it is speaking of an unblemished one, and [the verse] excludes it from the category of “its animals”; evidently it is the priest’s property. And this too is explained like the first version: since it was necessary to write “its animals” and it could not be derived from “its spoil,” learn from it that the priest has acquisition in it during its lifetime.

notes.he: למעוטי לבכור ומעשר תיפוק לי בכור ומעשר נמי משללה ולא שלל שמים. אלא מדאיצטריך בהמתה לבכור ש"מ דאית ליה זכייה בגויה והכי קאמר בהמתה המיוחד לה שאין בה לגבוה כלום ושרפת פרט לבהמת בכור וקשיא לרב נחמן:
notes.en: Why do I need “its animals”? To exclude the firstborn and tithe; derive the firstborn and tithe too from “its spoil,” and not the spoils of Heaven. Rather, since “its animals” was needed for the firstborn, learn from it that he has acquisition in it. And this is what it means: “its animals,” those that are particularly its own, in which the Most High has nothing, “and you shall burn,” excluding an animal of firstborn and tithe. And this is difficult for Rav Naḥman.

messages.text: Actually, the baraita is speaking of a blemished animal. And as for that which is difficult for you, that this is considered “its animals,” one can answer that this term includes only that which is eaten in the manner of its animals, without additional restrictions. This excludes even a blemished firstborn offering and animal tithe offering, which is not included in the category of “its animals.”

notes.he: ודקא קשיא לך היינו בהמתה מי שנאכל בתורת בהמתה. בחולין ושרפת יצא בכור ומעשר כדתנן כו':
notes.en: Actually with a blemished one. And as for what is difficult for you, this is “its animals”: [it means] that which is eaten in the manner of “its animals,” as non-sacred meat, “and you shall burn”; the firstborn and tithe are excluded, as we learned, etc.

messages.text: All disqualified consecrated animals are redeemed and then sold in the butchers’ market [ba’itliz], where they fetch a higher price, in order to benefit the Temple treasury. And they are slaughtered in the butchers’ market, and their meat is weighed and sold by the litra, as is done with non-sacred meat, with the exception of a firstborn offering and animal tithe offering, as their benefit is accrued to their owners. The money will benefit their owners rather than the Temple treasury, and private individuals may not disgrace disqualified offerings by treating them as one would non-sacred meat.
messages.lead: And which restrictions apply to the consumption of blemished firstborn animals? The restrictions are as we learned in a mishna:

messages.text: If one takes an oath falsely denying possession of another’s property, he must pay the value of that property and an additional one-fifth to the owner. The passage stating this halakha begins: “If anyone sin, and commit a trespass against the Lord, and deal falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of pledge, or of robbery”. By stating: “And commit a trespass against the Lord,” the verse serves to include one who denies possession of offerings of lesser sanctity belonging to another, as they are the property of their owner, who has the right to consume their meat after the sacrifice. This is the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita:

verse.he: נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תֶחֱטָא וּמָעֲלָה מַעַל בַּיהֹוָה וְכִחֵשׁ בַּעֲמִיתוֹ בְּפִקָּדוֹן אוֹ־בִתְשׂוּמֶת יָד אוֹ בְגָזֵל אוֹ עָשַׁק אֶת־עֲמִיתוֹ׃
verse.en: When a person sins and commits a trespass against GOD—by dealing deceitfully with another in the matter of a deposit or a pledge, uncertain. or through robbery, or by defrauding another,

notes.he: שאם הפקיד שלמים או בכור או מעשר אצל חבירו וכפר ונשבע והודה משלם קרן וחומש וקרבן שבועת הפקדון לפי שהם ממונו וקרינא ביה וכחש בעמיתו:
notes.en: To include offerings of lesser sanctity: that if he deposited a peace offering, a firstborn or a tithe animal with his fellow, and the fellow denied it, swore, and then admitted, he pays the principal and a fifth and brings the offering for an oath about a deposit, since they are [the depositor’s] property, and we apply to it “and deal falsely with his neighbor.”

notes.he: שיש בהן לגבוה ולעמיתו ומביא עליהן קרבן אשם מעילה:
notes.en: To include offerings of lesser sanctity, which are their [owners’] property: in which the Most High and his fellow have a share, and he brings a guilt offering for misuse for them.

messages.text: The verse serves to include only one who denies possession of a peace offering of another, not other offerings of lesser sanctity.

notes.he: קאתי דודאי הן ממונו אבל מעשר לא דאיהו לאו ממונו הוא ולא יכול למוכרו חי ולא שחוט לא תם ולא בעל מום והכי מפרש בפרק ארבעה אבות נזיקין:
notes.en: Ben Azzai says, to include peace offerings: he comes [to include them], since they are certainly his property; but not tithe, since it is not his property, as he may not sell it, whether alive or slaughtered, whether unblemished or blemished. And so it is explained in the chapter Arba’a Avot of Nezikin [Bava Kamma].

notes.he: מאי ממעט בן עזאי ממעט מעשר הואיל ואינו נמכר לא חשיב ממונו:
notes.en: Ben Azzai says, to include peace offerings. What does Ben Azzai exclude? He excludes tithe: since it is not sold, it is not considered his property.

messages.text: Ben Azzai stated his halakha only with regard to a firstborn offering, that it is considered the property of the owner, i.e., the priest, but not with regard to other offerings of lesser sanctity.

notes.dh: לא אמר בן עזאי אלא בבכור
notes.he: שהפקיד [כהן בכורו] אצל אחר וכפר ונשבע (והודה) אבל שלמים לא היה ממונו הואיל וחיילא עלייהו קדושה שטעונין סמיכה ונסכים ותנופת חזה ושוק ומעשר נמי לא הואיל ואינו יכול למוכרו והכי מפרש בפרק קמא דנזיקין (ב"ק דף יב:):
notes.en: Ben Azzai stated it only with regard to a firstborn: that [a priest] deposited [his firstborn] with another, who denied it and swore (and admitted). But peace offerings are not his property, since sanctity takes hold of them, as they require the laying on of hands, libations and the waving of the breast and thigh; nor is tithe, since he may not sell it. And so it is explained in the first chapter of Nezikin (Bava Kamma 12b).

notes.he: לא ריבה בן עזאי אלא בכור בלבד הואיל ונמכר תמים חי הוי ממונו [והא מפורש בבבא קמא בפרק ראשון]:
notes.en: Abba Yosei ben Dosai says: Ben Azzai included only the firstborn alone: since it is sold unblemished while alive, it is his property. [And this is explained in Bava Kamma, in the first chapter.]

messages.text: What era are we dealing with in this baraita? If we say it is in the present, doesn’t the baraita teach the halakha of a firstborn offering as similar to the halakha of a peace offering? Peace offerings are not a relevant category in the present day. Rather, it is obvious that the baraita is referring to the period when the Temple is standing.
messages.quote: only with regard to a firstborn offering

notes.he: ושלמים בזמן הזה ליכא:
notes.en: But it teaches it like peace offerings: and there are no peace offerings in the present.

notes.dh: אילימא בזמן הזה והא דומיא דשלמים קתני
notes.he: ובפ"ק דב"ק (דף יב:) פרש"י דבזמן בית המקדש איירי דהא קרא בשבועת הפקדון איירי בזמן בית המקדש הוא דמחייבין ליה אשם ונראה דמש"ה נקט הכא דומיא דשלמים ולא רצה לומר כדפרש"י בב"ק (שם) משום דבלאו הכי צריך לומר דומיא דשלמים כדי להוכיח דבתם איירי ולא בבעל מום כדאמרינן בסמוך:
notes.en: If we say in the present, but it teaches it like peace offerings: In the first chapter of Bava Kamma (12b) Rashi explained that it speaks of the time of the Temple because the verse about an oath concerning a deposit speaks of the time of the Temple, since that is when one is obligated to bring a guilt offering. And it seems that this is why [the Gemara] here uses “like peace offerings,” and did not want to say it as Rashi explained in Bava Kamma: because in any case it needs to say “like peace offerings” to prove that it speaks of an unblemished animal and not a blemished one, as we say shortly.

notes.he: אבא יוסי ושלמים אינה אלא בזמן בית המקדש:
notes.en: But it teaches it like peace offerings: [this is] Abba Yosei; and peace offerings exist only when the Temple is standing.

messages.text: And what type of animal are we dealing with? If we say that the baraita is referring specifically to a blemished animal, doesn’t it teach the halakha of a firstborn offering as similar to the halakha of a peace offering? Peace offerings are the property of their owners even when they are unblemished.

notes.dh: דאי בבעל מום הא דומיא דשלמים קתני
notes.he: ושלמים ודאי שלמים תמימים קא מרבי דממונן הוא דאין בהן מעילה מחיים דבשלמא בבכור גבי כהן איכא לפלוגי בין תם לבעל מום משום דתם איכא למימר לא זכי ביה כהן אלא משלחן גבוה והיינו מהקטרת אימורים ובעל מום דלית ביה הקרבה זכי ליה רחמנא מיד אבל גבי שלמים דישראל ליכא למימר ישראל משלחן גבוה זכי הלכך לא שנא תמין לא שנא בעלי מומין מחיים זכי בהו:
notes.en: For if with a blemished one, it teaches it like peace offerings: and with peace offerings it certainly includes unblemished peace offerings, which are [their owner’s] property, since there is no misuse of consecrated property with them during their lifetime. For granted, with a priest’s firstborn one can distinguish between an unblemished one and a blemished one: with an unblemished one one can say that the priest acquires it only from the table of the Most High, that is, from the burning of the sacrificial portions, while a blemished one, which is not sacrificed, the Merciful One grants him immediately. But with an Israelite’s peace offerings one cannot say that the Israelite acquires them from the table of the Most High. Therefore, whether unblemished or blemished, he acquires them during their lifetime.

messages.text: Rather, is it not referring even to an unblemished firstborn animal? And the baraita teaches that this animal is the property of its owner. Learn from it that the priest has the right of acquisition to an unblemished firstborn offering when the Temple is standing.

notes.he: וקא מיחייב לכופר [בבכור] קרבן שבועה אלמא ממונא דכהן הוא (ובבכור):
notes.en: Rather, is it not with an unblemished one: and it makes one who denies [having a firstborn] liable to the offering for an oath; evidently it is the priest’s property.

messages.text: 8b

No, actually, the baraita is referring to an unblemished animal when the Temple is standing, but it is speaking of a firstborn offering outside of Eretz Yisrael, and it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who said: If unblemished firstborn offerings came from outside of Eretz Yisrael, they may be sacrificed on the altar.
messages.quote: Rather, is it not referring even to an unblemished firstborn animal?

notes.he: ולא קשיא לרב נחמן דהאי דזכי ביה כהן מחיים בבכור בחוצה לארץ עסקינן דסתמיה לאו להקרבה קאי אפי' בזמן בית המקדש ודומיא דשלמים הוא דאי מייתי ליה מצי לאקרוביה אבל סתמיה לאו להקרבה קאי:
notes.en: Actually with an unblemished one: and it is not difficult for Rav Naḥman, for where the priest acquires it during its lifetime, we are dealing with a firstborn outside the Land, which ordinarily does not stand for sacrifice, even when the Temple is standing. And it is like peace offerings, in that if he brings it he may sacrifice it, but ordinarily it does not stand for sacrifice.

notes.he: דאמר לקמן בפ' אלו קדשים (תמורה דף כא.) אם באו בכורות תמימים מחוצה לארץ יקרבו אם באו אין לכתחילה לא:
notes.en: And it is Rabbi Shimon: who says below in the chapter Elu Kodashim (Temurah 21a): If unblemished firstborns came from outside the Land, they are sacrificed. If they came, yes; at the outset, no.

notes.dh: ורבי שמעון היא דאמר אם באו תמימים יקרבו
notes.he: אבל לכתחילה לא וטעמא משום דיש להם פרנסה במקומם ורבי עקיבא פליג ואמר דאפילו דיעבד לא יקרבו ומפרש טעמא משום דאיתקש בכור למעשר בהמה ומעשר בהמה למעשר דגן מה מעשר דגן אינו בא מחוצה לארץ לארץ ישראל אף בכור ומעשר כו' וא"ת אמאי לא אוקמא כר' עקיבא דלדידיה הוי טפי ממונו וי"ל דלר' עקיבא לא הויא כל כך דומיא דשלמים:
notes.en: And it is Rabbi Shimon, who said: If unblemished ones came, they are sacrificed: but not at the outset. And the reason is that they have their support in their own place. Rabbi Akiva disagrees and says that even after the fact they are not sacrificed, and he explains the reason: because the firstborn is juxtaposed to the animal tithe, and the animal tithe to the grain tithe; just as the grain tithe is not brought from outside the Land to Eretz Yisrael, so too the firstborn and the tithe, etc. And if you say: why did [the Gemara] not establish it according to Rabbi Akiva, for whom it is all the more his property? One can say that according to Rabbi Akiva it is not so much like peace offerings.

notes.he: הא דומיא דשלמים קתני דמצי קרבי אמר רבינא לעולם דבזמן בית המקדש קיים אפילו הכי לא קשיא לרב נחמן דהכא באיזה בכור קתני אבא יוסי דהוי ממונו דמצי זבין ליה בבכור הבא מחוצה לארץ לארץ ואליבא דר' שמעון דאמר (לקמן בפרק אלו קדשים) [בבבא קמא] אם באו תמימים מחוצה לארץ יקרבו אם באו אין אבל לכתחלה (לא) אין חייבין [להביאן] ולהקריבן הואיל והוא כן שאין חייב לכתחלה להביאן ולהקריבן הלכך הוי ממונו ומצי מזבין ליה אבל בכור דארץ ישראל דבעי מקריב ליה לא מצי מזבין ליה כרב נחמן:
notes.en: Rather, it is obvious, etc. But it teaches it like peace offerings, which can be sacrificed. Ravina said [our text has Abaye]: Actually, when the Temple is standing, and even so it is not difficult for Rav Naḥman. For here, which firstborn does Abba Yosei teach is his property, such that he can sell it? A firstborn that comes from outside the Land to the Land, and according to Rabbi Shimon, who said (below, in the chapter Elu Kodashim) [in Bava Kamma]: If unblemished ones came from outside the Land, they are sacrificed. If they came, yes; but at the outset one is (not) obligated [to bring them] and sacrifice them. Since it is so, that one is not obligated at the outset to bring them and sacrifice them, it is therefore his property and he can sell it. But a firstborn of Eretz Yisrael, which he must sacrifice, he cannot sell, as Rav Naḥman [said].

messages.text: This language indicates that there is no obligation to sacrifice such an animal, as people did not generally bring their firstborn offerings from outside Eretz Yisrael. Therefore, a priest is able to acquire it even when it is unblemished. Firstborn offerings from Eretz Yisrael, by contrast, cannot be acquired by the priests.

What is this comparison for me? If a priest does not substitute for a sin offering and a guilt offering, which priests do not acquire during the animals’ lifetimes, will you say the same with regard to a firstborn, which priests acquire during the animal’s lifetime?
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection from the mishna:

messages.text: What are we dealing with in the mishna? If we say that it is referring to a blemished animal, isn’t the mishna saying that the firstborn offering is similar to a sin offering and a guilt offering, which the priests acquire only unblemished? Rather, is it not referring to unblemished animals? And it nevertheless teaches: Which priests acquire during the animal’s lifetime.
messages.quote: a firstborn, which priests acquire during the animal’s lifetime

notes.he: והאי חטאת ואשם בתמימים קמיירי דקתני אין זוכין בהן הכהנים בחייהן אבל לאחר שחיטה זוכין אלמא בבני הקרבה עסקינן:
notes.en: It speaks of it like a sin offering and a guilt offering: and this sin offering and guilt offering are unblemished ones, since it teaches that the priests do not acquire them during their lifetime, but after slaughter they do acquire them; evidently we are dealing with animals fit for sacrifice.

messages.text: This mishna too is referring to a firstborn offering outside of Eretz Yisrael, and it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who said: If unblemished firstborn offerings came from outside of Eretz Yisrael, they may be sacrificed on the altar. The priests do not acquire firstborn offerings from Eretz Yisrael.
Let us say that acquisition of the firstborn offerings by the priests is the subject of a dispute between tanna’im.

notes.he: אי זכי כהן בבכור תם מחיים בזמן בית המקדש אי לא:
notes.en: Let us say it is a dispute between tanna’im: whether the priest acquires an unblemished firstborn during its lifetime when the Temple is standing, or not.

messages.text: In the case of a firstborn offering, when it is in the house of its owner, who did not yet give it to a priest, its owner can render another animal a substitute for it. Once it is in the house of the priest, its owner cannot render a substitute for it.
Once it has entered the possession of the priest, its owner cannot render a substitute for it.
Apparently, the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar is identical to that of the first tanna. What is their dispute?
messages.quote: Once it has entered the possession of the priest

notes.he: תנא קמא:
notes.en: What, is it not that this is what he is saying: the first tanna.

messages.text: What, is it not correct that this is what the first tanna is saying: Once it is in the house, i.e., possession, of the priest, the priest can render a substitute for it, but the owner cannot render a substitute for it, as the priest has acquired it; while Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds that once it enters the possession of the priest, neither of them can render a substitute with it. Apparently, the first tanna holds that the priest has the right of acquisition to an unblemished firstborn offering when the Temple is standing.
messages.quote: Once it is in the house of the priest, its owner cannot render a substitute for it

notes.he: תנא קמא בבית כהן אינו עושה תמורה על ידי בעלים אלא על ידי כהן אבל כהן ממיר בו דאית ליה זכייה בגויה:
notes.en: What, is it not that this is what he is saying: the first tanna [means]: in the priest’s house no substitute is rendered by the owners, but by the priest; for the priest does substitute with it, since he has acquisition in it.

notes.he: אין עושה תמורה לבעלים קאמר אבל כהן עושה תמורה ומדכהן עושה תמורה אלמא מצי מזבין ליה ור' שמעון בן אלעזר סבר כיון שבא ליד כהן אין עושה תמורה אפי' כהן דלא זכי ביה והיינו כרב נחמן:
notes.en: In the house of a priest: he is saying that the owners do not render a substitute, but the priest does render a substitute; and since the priest renders a substitute, evidently he can sell it. And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds that once it has come into the hands of a priest no substitute is rendered, even by the priest, since he does not acquire it; and this accords with Rav Naḥman.

messages.text: The opinion of the first tanna is not difficult; one can say that the dispute in the baraita concerns a firstborn offering outside of Eretz Yisrael, while those from Eretz Yisrael are not acquired by the priests. And this opinion of the first tanna accords with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri in the mishna above, and that opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar accords with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva in that mishna.

notes.he:
בפלוגתא דרבי יוחנן בן נורי ורבי עקיבא דמתני' קא מיפלגי וההיא הא אוקימנא בבכור בחוצה לארץ וקאמר תנא קמא כהן עושה בו תמורה משבא לידו דהא זכי ביה מחיים דסתמיה לאו להקרבה כרבי יוחנן בן נורי ור' שמעון כר' עקיבא דאע"ג דאית ליה זכייה בגוויה אינו עושה תמורה על ידו דנפקא ליה מהקישא כדמפרש במתני' היכן קדושה חלה עליו כו'.
ע"א עושה תמורה דישראל והכהן אינו עושה תמורה לא זה ולא זה:
notes.en: No: they disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and Rabbi Akiva in our mishna, and that one we have established as a firstborn outside the Land. And the first tanna says that the priest renders a substitute with it once it has come into his hands, since he acquires it during its lifetime, as it ordinarily does not stand for sacrifice, like Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri. And Rabbi Shimon is like Rabbi Akiva: even though [the priest] has acquisition in it, no substitute is rendered by him, since [Rabbi Akiva] derives it from the juxtaposition, as explained in the mishna: “Where does the sanctity take effect on it,” etc. [The note ends with a short, cryptic gloss, apparently on the baraita’s wording:] “They render a substitute”: of the Israelite; “and the priest does not render a substitute”: neither this one nor that one.

notes.dh: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר כו' זה וזה
notes.he:
כהן וישראל. מאי לאו דרב נחמן איכא בינייהו דהאי דקאמר תנא קמא אצל כהן אינו עושה תמורה דאית ביה זכייה בגוויה כרב נחמן ורבי שמעון לית ליה דרב נחמן לא דכולי עלמא לית להו דרב נחמן בבכור מעליא והכא בפלוגתא דרבי יוחנן בן נורי ורבי עקיבא פליגי ובבכור בחוצה לארץ ולהכי אמר ת"ק דכהן אין עושה בו תמורה ור' שמעון כר' עקיבא.
ל"א לימא כתנאי בכור אצל כהן אינו עושה תמורה לא ישראל ולא כהן ואמרי הכי מימר הוא דלא מימר הא זבוני מזבין ליה רבי שמעון בר אלעזר אומר כיון שבא ליד כהן זה וזה אינו עושה תמורה כלומר דאפילו זבוני לא מצי מזבין ליה דכל תנא בתרא לטפויי מילתא קאתי מאי לאו דרב נחמן איכא בינייהו דתנא קמא אית ליה דרב נחמן ור' אלעזר לית ליה דרב נחמן:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, etc., this one and that one [Rashi’s text of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar’s words reads “neither this one nor that one renders a substitute,” where the English above has “its owner”]: the priest and the Israelite. What, is it not that Rav Naḥman’s [ruling] is the difference between them: that what the first tanna says, that with the priest no substitute is rendered [by the owner] since [the priest] has acquisition in it, is “like Rav Naḥman,” and Rabbi Shimon does not hold Rav Naḥman’s [view]? No: all agree in not holding Rav Naḥman’s [view] with a proper firstborn, and here they disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and Rabbi Akiva, with a firstborn outside the Land; and that is why the first tanna said that the priest does not render a substitute with it, and Rabbi Shimon is like Rabbi Akiva. Another version: Let us say it is a dispute between tanna’im: a firstborn with a priest has no substitute rendered for it, neither by the Israelite nor by the priest. And we say: it is substituting that he may not do, but he may sell it. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Once it has come into the priest’s hands, neither this one nor that one renders a substitute; that is to say, he may not even sell it, since each later tanna comes to add something. What, is it not that Rav Naḥman’s [ruling] is the difference between them: the first tanna holds Rav Naḥman’s [view], and Rabbi [Shimon ben] Elazar does not hold Rav Naḥman’s [view]? [So the printed text reads in both versions, although by the Gemara’s reasoning above it is the first tanna who holds that the priest acquires the firstborn.]

notes.dh: לא בפלוגתא דרבי יוחנן בן נורי ורבי עקיבא דמתני' קמפלגי
notes.he: כלומר וההוא אוקימנא בבכור חוצה לארץ:
notes.en: No, they disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and Rabbi Akiva in our mishna: that is to say, and that one we established as a firstborn outside the Land.

notes.dh: לא הני תנאי בפלוגתא דר' יוחנן בן נורי ור' עקיבא קא מיפלגי
notes.he: דתנא קמא דאמר בבית כהן אין עושה תמורה לבעלי' אלא לכהן סבר כר' יוחנן בן נורי ר' שמעון בן אלעזר סבר כר' עקיבא. לישנ' אחרינא אצל ישראל עושין תמורה [משמע השתא להאי לישנא דעד שהוא ברשות ישראל אפילו כהן מימר בו לטעמיה דר' שמעון בן אלעזר דאמר כיון שבא ליד כהן זה וזה אין מימר מכלל דאצל ישראל זה וזה ממירין בו אלמא אית ליה זכייה בגויה. ותנא קמא דאמר אצל ישראל עושין תמורה] משמע לישראל ולא לכהן והיינו כרב נחמן [לא בפלוגתא כו']:
notes.en: No, these tanna’im disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and Rabbi Akiva. The first tanna, who said that in the house of a priest no substitute is rendered by the owners but [it is] by the priest, holds like Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri; Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds like Rabbi Akiva. Another version: with an Israelite a substitute is rendered. [Now according to this version, it implies that while it is in the Israelite’s domain even a priest may substitute with it, following the reasoning of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, who said that once it has come into a priest’s hands neither this one nor that one substitutes: by implication, with an Israelite both substitute with it; evidently he has acquisition in it. And the first tanna, who said that with an Israelite a substitute is rendered,] implies by the Israelite and not by the priest, and this accords with Rav Naḥman. [No, in the dispute, etc.]

messages.caption: Does the priest acquire an unblemished firstborn while the Temple stands? The six challenges to Rav Naḥman on 8a–8b and how each is answered.

messages.text: The Sages taught this halakha only with regard to a priest selling to a priest, but with regard to a priest selling it to an Israelite, it is prohibited even when the animal is alive.
messages.lead: The Gemara earlier (7b) cited a mishna (Ma’aser Sheni 1:2) which states that a firstborn offering may be sold unblemished only while it is alive.

notes.he: יכול למוכרו תמים:
notes.en: They taught this only of a priest to a priest: he may sell it unblemished.

messages.text: What is the reason? Since an Israelite can consume a firstborn animal only if it is blemished, there is a concern that perhaps the Israelite will go and inflict a blemish on the firstborn offering and bring it to a halakhic authority to attain permission to eat it, and he will say to him: A priest gave me this firstborn offering when it was already blemished.

notes.dh: בכור זה נתן לי כהן במומו
notes.he: אבל כהן לכהן ליכא למימר הכי דכהן המביא בכור להראותו לחכם צריך להביא עדים שנפל בו אותו מום מאליו דאמרינן בבכורות בפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לה.) כל מומין הראוין לבא בידי אדם רועי ישראל נאמנים רועי כהנים אינם נאמנים דנחשדו כהנים על הבכורות:
notes.en: A priest gave me this firstborn with its blemish: but with a priest to a priest one cannot say this, since a priest who brings a firstborn to show a halakhic authority must bring witnesses that the blemish befell it by itself. As we say in Bekhorot, in the chapter Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 35a): with all blemishes that can be caused by a person, Israelite herdsmen are trusted and priestly herdsmen are not trusted, since priests were suspected regarding firstborns.

notes.he: דלמא אזיל ישראל ושדי ביה מומא וממטי ליה (לחבריה) [לחכם] ואמר בכור זה נתן לי כהן במומו - ואם תאמר מאי בכך והא לא שרו ליה כיון דנפק המום מיד כהן בלא עדים שהרי נחשדו הכהנים על זה ויש לומר דהכי קאמר נתן לי כהן במומו וקמי דידי נפל בו מום מאליו וא"ת היכי חייש דלמא אזיל ישראל ושדי ביה מומא והרי לא נחשדו ישראל על כך כדאמרינן בבכורות (דף לה.) דבכור ביד ישראל הכל נאמנין עליו דכהנים הוא דחשידי אמומי אבל ישראל לא חשידי ואין לומר דה"מ בודאי בכור היכא דסופו ליתנו לכהן דאין ישראל חוטא ולא לו דהא בפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לה:) אמר רב נחמן גבי ספק בכור בעליו מעידין עליו ויש לומר דלא דמי דה"מ כשהיה תם תחילה ביד ישראל אז ירא להטיל בו מום מאחר שנולד ברשותו דאין לו להשמט בשום דבר אבל הכא דיש לו לתלות שנתן לו הכהן במומו יש לחשדו עליו ונראה דלכך לא רצה לומר בענין אחר דלמא אזיל ישראל ושדי ביה מומא ומראהו לחכם ואמר דמעצמו נפל ולא יאמר כהן נתנו לי דכה"ג לא עביד דלמא יחשדוהו עליו ולומר מה לו לטרוח עליו ולהביאו לחכם כיון דלאו דידיה הוא ופריך והא אמר רב יהודה אין רואין בכור לישראל אלא אם כן כהן עמו והטעם שמא יעכבנו לעצמו ולא יתננו לכהן וכיון דצריך להביא הכהן לא מצי אמר בכור זה נתנו כהן במומו דאמרינן ליה אייתי (ראייה) ההוא כהן דיהבא לך דכל כמה דלא אייתי ליה לא שרינן ליה הבכור:
notes.en: Perhaps the Israelite will go and inflict a blemish on it, bring it (to his fellow) [to a halakhic authority] and say: A priest gave me this firstborn with its blemish: And if you say: what of it? They would not permit it to him, since the blemish came out of a priest’s hands without witnesses, for the priests were suspected of this. One can say that this is what he means: A priest gave it to me with its blemish, and before me the blemish befell it on its own. And if you say: how is there a concern that perhaps the Israelite will go and inflict a blemish on it? But Israelites are not suspected of this, as we say in Bekhorot (35a) that regarding a firstborn in an Israelite’s possession all are trusted, since it is the priests who are suspected about blemishes, but Israelites are not suspected. And one cannot say that this applies only to a definite firstborn, which he must eventually give to a priest, since an Israelite does not sin when it brings him nothing; for in the chapter Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 35b) Rav Naḥman said regarding an uncertain firstborn that its owners may testify about it. One can say that it is not comparable: that applies where it was unblemished at first in the Israelite’s possession; then he is afraid to inflict a blemish on it, since it was born in his domain and he has no way to slip out of [suspicion]. But here, where he can attribute it to the priest having given it to him with its blemish, he is to be suspected. And it seems that this is why [the Gemara] did not want to put it another way, that perhaps the Israelite will go and inflict a blemish on it and show it to a halakhic authority and say that it occurred by itself, without saying “a priest gave it to me”: in such a case he would not do so, lest they suspect him and say, why does he trouble himself over it and bring it to a halakhic authority, since it is not his? And [the Gemara] asks: But didn’t Rav Yehuda [our text of the Gemara: Rav] say: One does not examine a firstborn for an Israelite unless a priest is with him? And the reason is lest he keep it for himself and not give it to a priest. And since he must bring the priest, he cannot say, “A priest gave me this firstborn with its blemish,” for we tell him: Bring that priest who gave it to you; as long as he does not bring him, we do not permit the firstborn to him.

notes.he: ל"א אי שרית ליה לזבוני לישראל דילמא מעכב ליה ישראל לבכור דהוי בתוך עדריה עד דנפיל ביה מומא ואמר בכור זה מכר לי כהן במומו ומשתמיט ליה ולא יהיב בכורו לכהן:
notes.en: Another version: if you permit him to sell it to an Israelite, perhaps the Israelite will hold back the firstborn that is in his own flock until a blemish befalls it, and say: A priest sold me this firstborn with its blemish; and so he will slip out of it and not give his firstborn to a priest.

messages.text: And may a halakhic authority permit the animal in a case such as this?
messages.quote: A priest gave me this firstborn offering when it was already blemished

notes.he: אפי' הוי מום קבוע ומי שרי חכם את הבכור לישראל בלא כהן עמו:
notes.en: And may a halakhic authority permit it so: even if it is a permanent blemish, may a halakhic authority permit the firstborn to an Israelite without a priest with him?

messages.text: A halakhic authority may not look at a firstborn offering brought by an Israelite to determine if it has the type of permanent blemish allowing it to be slaughtered unless a priest is with him, out of concern that the Israelite will keep the blemished animal for himself without performing the mitzva of giving it to a priest.
messages.lead: But didn’t Rav say:

notes.he: דשמא כשידע זה שמום קבוע הוא דלא הוי קדשים בחוץ אכיל ליה ולא חייש לגזילה דכהן הלכך בעינן כהן בהדיה ולא מצי למימר בכור זה נתן לי כהן במומו דאמרינן ליה אייתי לי ההוא כהן דיהביה לך דכל כמה דלא אייתי ליה לא שרינן ליה הבכור אלא א"כ יהיב ליה כהן:
notes.en: Unless a priest is with him: for perhaps, when this one knows that it is a permanent blemish, so that it is no longer [a case of] consecrated animals [slaughtered] outside [the Temple], he will eat it and not worry about robbing the priest. Therefore we require a priest with him, and he cannot say, “A priest gave me this firstborn with its blemish,” since we tell him: Bring me that priest who gave it to you. As long as he does not bring him, we do not permit the firstborn to him unless a priest gave it to him.

notes.he: אין רואין בכור לישראל כשבא ואמר בכור זה נתן לי כהן במומו:
notes.en: One does not examine a firstborn for an Israelite: when he comes and says, “A priest gave me this firstborn with its blemish.”

notes.dh: ומי מצי למימר הכי והא אמר רב יהודה כו'
notes.he: (דראשית הוא בכור):
notes.en: And can he say this? But didn’t Rav Yehuda [our text: Rav] say, etc. [A marginal note in the printed edition suggests reading: unless a priest is with him and admits that the firstborn belongs to the Israelite.] (As “the first” is the firstborn.) [This last phrase is unclear in the printed text.]

messages.text: If so, one can demand that the priest who sold him the animal must be present, and this should prevent the Israelite from lying about the blemish.

This is the reason why it is prohibited for a priest to sell an unblemished firstborn offering to an Israelite: Because this looks like a priest who assists at the threshing floor in order to receive teruma from an Israelite. Unblemished firstborn offerings have a low purchase price, as the owner must wait for it to become blemished before eating it. It might appear that the priest sold the animal to an Israelite at a discount in order to receive future firstborns from him.
messages.lead: Rav Huna, son of Rabbi Yehoshua, said:

notes.he: לקנות בכור תם מן הכהן משום דסתם בכור תם בזמן הזה נמכר בזול דבעי לוקח לשהוייה עד שיומם הילכך הוה האי כהן דמוזיל גבי ישראל נראה ככהן המסייע בבית הגרנות לזרות ולעמר כדי שיתנו לו התרומות והוי חילול השם דמחזי כמאן דשקיל לתרומה בתורת שכירות והאי כהן נמי מיחזי דמשום הכי מוזיל לישראל כי היכי דליתיב ליה בכורות שיוולדו לו בעדרו:
notes.en: This is the reason it is forbidden to an Israelite: to buy an unblemished firstborn from the priest: because an unblemished firstborn in the present is ordinarily sold cheaply, since the buyer must keep it until it is blemished. Therefore this priest who lowers the price for an Israelite looks like a priest who assists at the threshing floors, winnowing and binding sheaves, so that they will give him the terumot; and it is a desecration of God’s name, for it looks like one who takes teruma as wages. And this priest too looks as though he lowers the price for the Israelite for this reason, so that he will give him the firstborns that will be born in his flock.

notes.dh: לשון רש"י היינו טעמא דנראה ככהן המסייע בבית הגרנות
notes.he: דרגילות הוא דמוכר בכור דמוזיל גבי [ישראל] כדי שיתן לו בכור פעם אחרת וכל שכן דאסור לקבלו במתנה וצריך ליזהר שאם אמר ישראל לכהן הילך בכור זה אם אמר לו הכהן שלך יהא אז אסור לקבלו מפני שנראה ככהן המסייע בבית הגרנות:
notes.en: Rashi’s wording: This is the reason, because it looks like a priest who assists at the threshing floor: for it is common that one who sells a firstborn lowers the price for [an Israelite] so that he will give him a firstborn another time; and all the more so it is forbidden to receive it as a gift. And one must be careful: if an Israelite said to a priest, “Here is this firstborn,” and the priest said to him, “Let it be yours,” then it is forbidden to receive it, because it looks like a priest who assists at the threshing floor.

notes.he: שיאמר אני נתתיו לו במומו וכהן לכהן מוכר משום דאין הכהן נאמן ע"י עצמו אלא היינו טעמא דלישראל אסור מפני שנראה ככהן המסייע [בבית הגרנות מה כהן המסייע בבית הגרנות אין נותנין תרומה מפני שנראה כאלו נותנו לו בשכרו אף כהן שמוכר בכורו לישראל נראה כמוכרו לו בזול בשביל שכשיולד לו בכור שיתנהו לו ולא לאחר אסור]:
notes.en: Unless a priest was [with him]: who would say, “I gave it to him with its blemish.” And a priest sells to a priest, since the priest is not trusted on his own [word]. Rather, this is the reason it is forbidden to an Israelite: because it looks like a priest who assists [at the threshing floor]. [Just as to a priest who assists at the threshing floors teruma is not given, because it looks as though they give it to him as his wages, so too a priest who sells his firstborn to an Israelite looks as though he sells it to him cheaply so that, when a firstborn is born to him, he will give it to him and not to another; it is forbidden.]

messages.text: The Aramaic names him Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua (רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע); the English translation has “son of Rabbi Yehoshua.”
Mar Zutra arrived at the home of Rav Ashi.
Let the Master taste some food.
messages.lead: Those present said to him:

messages.text: They brought meat before him.
Let the Master eat, as this meat is particularly healthful, because it is a firstborn.
messages.lead: The one who placed the meat before him said:

notes.he: שבשר בכור בריאה לאכול משאר הבשר:
notes.en: Let the Master eat, for it is healthful: for the meat of a firstborn is healthier to eat than other meat.

notes.he: שהוא ברי ושמן יותר מאחרים:
notes.en: Mavrei: that it is healthier and fatter than others.

messages.text: From where did you receive this firstborn animal?

notes.he: מי נתנו לכם הא אינכם כהנים:
notes.en: From where do you have this: who gave it to you? You are not priests.

messages.text: It is an animal that so-and-so the priest sold to us.
messages.lead: They said to him:

messages.text: Do you not hold like that which Rav Huna, son of Rabbi Yehoshua, said, that Israelites may not receive an unblemished firstborn offering from a priest because it looks like a priest who assists at the threshing floor?
messages.lead: Mar Zutra said to them:
messages.quote: looks like a priest who assists at the threshing floor

notes.he: דאסור לקנות בשר בכור מכהן דלמא מוזיל גבייכו ונראה ככהן המסייע:
notes.en: And do you not hold: that it is forbidden to buy the meat of a firstborn from a priest, lest he lower the price for you, and it looks like a priest who assists?

messages.text: We hold that this is not a concern, as we purchased it for its fair market value, and did not receive it at a discount. Therefore, there is no appearance of impropriety.
messages.lead: They said to Mar Zutra:

notes.he: וליכא למיחש למסייע דהא לא יהיב לן במתנה:
notes.en: We are buying it: and there is no concern of [his being one who] assists, since he did not give it to us as a gift.

messages.text: But do you not hold like that which we learned in a mishna:
messages.lead: Mar Zutra said to them:

messages.text: Until when is an Israelite obligated to tend to a firstborn animal before giving it to the priest? In the case of a small animal, a sheep or goat, thirty days, and in the case of a large animal, one of a herd of cattle, fifty days. And if the priest said to the owner: Give it to me within its period, the owner may not give it to him.

notes.he: לטרוח בו לגדלו קודם שיתננו לכהן:
notes.en: To tend: to take trouble over it, raising it, before he gives it to the priest.

messages.text: And Rav Sheshet says: What is the reason for this? Because it looks like a priest who assists at the threshing floor, as the priest is assisting the Israelite by assuming the responsibility of tending to the firstborn.

notes.he: דהשתא הוי סיוע שמצילו מלטרוח בו בלבד שיתננו לו:
notes.en: Like a priest who assists: for this now is assistance, that he saves him from the trouble of it, only so that he will give it to him.

messages.text: There the circumstances of the matter prove that the priest accepted responsibility to care for the animal in return for some benefit, and it has the appearance of impropriety. Here, we purchased it for its fair market value, and there is no appearance of impropriety.
messages.lead: They said to Mar Zutra:

notes.he: דהא מסייע הוא שהרי מיד מצילו מן הטורח והמזונות:
notes.en: The matter proves: that he is one who assists, for he immediately saves him from the trouble and the feeding.

notes.he: (הכא) [התם] במתניתין מוכחא מילתא דא"ל א"ל כהן בתוך הזמן [תנהו ולא יהיב ליה דמי מידי (כהן לישראל)] [ישראל לכהן] הילכך מיחזא ככהן המסייע [בבית הגרנות] דבההוא הנאה קא יהיב ליה ניהליה שפוטרו מטיפולו הכא כיון דמוכרו דיהבינן להון דמי לא מיחזי ככהן המסייע:
notes.en: They said to him: [There,] in the mishna, the matter proves itself, since [the priest] said to him within the period, [“Give it to me,” and he pays him nothing]; therefore it looks like a priest who assists [at the threshing floor], for it is through that benefit that he gives it to him, since he exempts him from tending it. Here, since he sells it and we give them money, it does not look like a priest who assists.

messages.text: There the Israelite does not give payment to the priest for accepting responsibility to care for the animal. Here, the Israelite gives payment to the priest, as we purchased the animal.
messages.lead: The Gemara presents an alternative version of this final response. They said to Mar Zutra:

notes.dh: לשון רש"י היינו טעמא דנראה ככהן המסייע בבית הגרנות
notes.he: דרגילות הוא דמוכר בכור דמוזיל גבי [ישראל] כדי שיתן לו בכור פעם אחרת וכל שכן דאסור לקבלו במתנה וצריך ליזהר שאם אמר ישראל לכהן הילך בכור זה אם אמר לו הכהן שלך יהא אז אסור לקבלו מפני שנראה ככהן המסייע בבית הגרנות:
notes.en: Rashi’s wording: This is the reason, because it looks like a priest who assists at the threshing floor: for it is common that one who sells a firstborn lowers the price for [an Israelite] so that he will give him a firstborn another time; and all the more so it is forbidden to receive it as a gift. And one must be careful: if an Israelite said to a priest, “Here is this firstborn,” and the priest said to him, “Let it be yours,” then it is forbidden to receive it, because it looks like a priest who assists at the threshing floor. [This note repeats, word for word, Tosafot’s note on Rav Huna’s statement above.]

messages.text: And what would you say to this claim? Would you say that perhaps the priest lowered the price of the animal for us, as the priest thinks that when we have another firstborn offering we will give it to him, and therefore it has the appearance of impropriety? This is not a concern, as he thinks:

notes.he: כי היכי דניתיב ליה בכורות דידן ולא לכהן אחר:
notes.en: What would you say, perhaps the priest lowers the price: so that he will give him our firstborns and not another priest.

notes.he: עביד הכי:
notes.en: No: he does not do so.

notes.he: דהשתא טב מקרא דלמחר. בוצינא דלעת קטנה קרא דלעת גדולה. כלומר מוטב שאמכרנו בשויו דשמא אם אני מניח להם מן הדמים לא יועילו לי כלום ולא יתנו לי בכורות שלהן:
notes.en: For he considers: a butzina now is better than a kara tomorrow. A butzina is a small gourd; a kara is a large gourd. That is to say: better that I sell it at its value, for perhaps if I leave them some of the price it will gain me nothing, and they will not give me their firstborns.

notes.he: מאי אמרת דלמא מוזיל כהן לגביה שנותנו לו בפחות מדמיו לא עביד דסבר בוצינא טב מקרא מוטב ריוח מועט שאטול עכשו שאמכרנו לו בשוויו מלפחות עכשו ובשביל ריוח של אחר זמן ל"א מר זוטרא כו'. אמרו ליה לא סבירא לן [דרב הונא] ועוד דהא מיזבן קא זבנינן אמר להו ולא סבירא לכו מתני' שאמרה כרב הונא בריה דרב יהושע אמרו ליה לא דמי דהתם מוכח מילתא כיון דיהב ליה בלא דמי אבל הכא מיזבן קא זבנינן ולא מיחזי ככהן המסייע:
notes.en: What would you say, perhaps the priest lowers the price for him, giving it to him for less than its value? He would not do so, since he thinks: a zucchini is better than a gourd. Better the small profit that I take now, selling it to him at its value, than to take less now for the sake of a later profit. Another version: Mar Zutra, etc. They said to him: We do not hold [like Rav Huna]; and further, we are buying it. He said to them: And do you not hold the mishna, which accords with Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua? They said to him: It is not comparable, for there the matter proves itself, since he gives it to him without payment; but here we are buying it, and it does not look like a priest who assists.

messages.text: Continues on 9a: “A zucchini now is better than a gourd later.” Then a new mishna lists the kinds of animals from which, and upon which, one may substitute.
